answer.text: Exchange-traded Indian listed equity, derivatives, ETFs (various rates)

explanation.text: The Logic: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied on transactions in specified Indian securities executed on recognised stock exchanges — principally listed equity shares (delivery and intraday), equity derivatives (futures and options), and equity-oriented ETFs. Rates vary by segment and transaction type. The Trap: STT does not apply to all securities globally, to unlisted securities transferred off-exchange, or to bank deposits — these are outside the scope of the STT regime. Note: The specific scope of STT across listed equity, derivatives, and ETFs is not laid out in the cited PMS workbook, which only references STT as a transaction cost and as not deductible for individuals. The framing above reflects the general Securities Transaction Tax Act / Finance Act provisions rather than a direct workbook citation.
